prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every Miami car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on your case details (severity of injuries, liability issues, insurance limits) and what you value (trial experience, communications style, fee structure). I can help you find strong candidates, but here are practical steps and criteria to pick the best lawyer for your situation.

How to find top Miami car-accident lawyers
- Use reputable directories and ratings: Florida Bar lawyer search, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, and local Google/Yelp reviews.  
- Ask for referrals from friends, family, or other attorneys (e.g., criminal or family lawyers).  
- Contact the Florida Bar’s Lawyer Referral Service for vetted referrals.

Key credentials and experience to look for
- Focus on lawyers who specialize in car-accident/personal-injury (not general practice).  
- Board certification in Civil Trial Law (Florida Board Certification) is a plus.  
- Substantial trial experience and a track record of verdicts and sizeable settlements.  
- Experience handling insurance companies, PIP issues, medical lien negotiation, and catastrophic-injury cases if applicable.  
- Good client references and clear communication practices.

Questions to ask at the initial consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases like mine (similar injuries/insurance limits)? Can you share sample settlements/verdicts?  
- Who will handle the day-to-day work (partner, associate, paralegal)?  
- What’s your fee (contingency %), and what costs will I owe if we don’t recover?  
- How do you communicate (phone/email/text), and how often will I get updates?  
- What is your estimated timeline and likely value range for my case?  
- Do you have expert witnesses you use (medical, accident reconstruction)?

Practical tips and red flags
- Most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency ranges are roughly 30–40% depending on whether suit is filed or the case goes to trial — ask for specifics in writing.  
- Get all fee agreements and retainer terms in writing.  
- Red flags: promises of a specific settlement amount, poor responsiveness during the interview, pressuring you to sign immediately, or no written fee agreement.

Important deadlines and procedural notes (Florida)
- Statute of limitations for most car-accident injury claims in Florida is 4 years from the accident (act promptly).  
- Florida also has PIP (no-fault) procedures — deadlines apply for PIP claims and medical documentation; an attorney can help navigate them.

If you’d like, I can:
- Look up top-rated personal-injury lawyers/firms in Miami (give me your ZIP code or neighborhood), or  
- Suggest 3–5 attorneys to contact based on your case details (injury severity, fault issues, any ongoing treatment).

Which would you prefer?
